name_reason: Name is fully compliant. Prefix data_fd2_battle_ is correct for a battle core table. The descriptor weapon_attack_anim_pattern_ptr_table accurately reflects both purpose (per-weapon attack-animation pattern pointers) and data type (pointer table). The _21 suffix is the array dimension (21 entries, indexed by weapon attack-pattern id 0..20), a meaningful domain/dimension marker, not Ghidra address residue: the address is 0x61955 and 21 (=0x15) matches no part of it; the companion pool symbol analogously carries a size suffix (_84b). Verified read-only via the sole reader fd2_get_attack_anim_pattern_for_weapon (asm MOV EAX,[EBX*4 + 0x61955]) with no writers.
purpose: Per-weapon-type attack-hit animation script pointer table: 21 entries indexed by weapon attack-pattern id (0..20), each pointing into the immediately following 84-byte script pool that holds the per-weapon swing animation byte-stream.
logic_summary: Const dword[21] table at 0x61955. Sole reader fd2_get_attack_anim_pattern_for_weapon @ 0x4E52D returns table[weapon_type] (SHL idx,2; MOV EAX,[idx+0x61955]). Returned pointer is consumed by fd2_animate_attack_hit_sequence @ 0x1E98C as a byte stream { step_count, (sprite_id, sfx_id)*step_count } (sfx 0xFF = silent). All 21 entries reference one of six distinct records inside data_fd2_battle_weapon_attack_anim_pattern_script_pool_84b @ 0x619A9 at offsets +0/+13/+26/+39/+56/+73; multiple weapon types share the same record. No writers anywhere -> const. Memory bytes verified byte-exact against the src initializer.
datatype: const uint8 *[21]  (21-entry array of pointers; each is a const byte-stream pointer into the 0x619A9 script pool)
element_semantics: Element i = pointer to the attack-hit animation script record for weapon attack-pattern id i (0..20). The pointed-to record is { step_count(byte), then step_count * (sprite_id byte, sfx_id byte) }; sfx_id 0xFF means no sound. Distinct record targets: idx 0/1/2/9/12/18 -> +0 (0x619A9); 3/10/17 -> +13 (0x619B6); 4 -> +26 (0x619C3); 5/11 -> +39 (0x619D0); 6/8/13/15/16/19/20 -> +56 (0x619E1); 7/14 -> +73 (0x619F2).
